items.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...that was a Lovie Austin record, wasn't it? ... No, Lovie Austin played it, but that's our record.

ctx.x: hearing your voice again. Well, I would be glad for you to play, for him to hear. Me and Mac. Yes, and we had, we were known in show business as Mary Mack's Merry Makers. Oh, yes.

Uh-huh. That record that you made with Kid Punch is called that, I remember. The Merry Makers Twine? Well, oh, that, no, that was a Lovie Austin record, wasn't it? No, Lovie Austin played it, but that's our record. I know. I mean, she made a record of it once. Yes. Oh, yes, she did. That's

quite a while back. Now, what did that mean, that Merry Makers Twine? Well, you can see here, this is the name of the company. We call it at first, the Southern Comedy Company, but after we got a little better organized and more people added to the show, we named it after the wife, Mary. Oh, yes.
